merged.title: fix(launcher): stop mod updates running into GitHub's API limit
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Updating the mods from openrac-mods stopped with "…/releases?per_page=100 could not be fetched (curl: (56) … error: 403)". Without a login GitHub's API allows 60 requests an hour per network. Reading a repository costs three requests (releases, commit, tree), and every mod's update read the same repository again. So checking openrac-mods' eleven mods and updating them all took 36 requests, and a second try ran out.

- GitHub API answers are now kept for five minutes for the whole launcher run (`remote::ApiCache` / `remote::Cached`, used by the Tauri mod and hub commands). A check followed by Update all on one repository now costs 3 requests instead of 36. Applying index mods from one repository reads its release list once.
- Pinned releases and a code's SUMS hash are now looked up in that same shared release list, and repository archives come from github.com's `/archive/` instead of the API zipball, so neither counts against the limit.
- curl no longer runs with `-f`, so the launcher c

merged.title: ci: build and test the Linux port in one job per game
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
Since #341 Going Commando has three programs, and on develop Port / Linux (checks) and the Windows and Android launcher builds ran into their hour with a cold cache and were cancelled (runs 42315643500 and 42315374502). The PR run of the same code passed Port / Linux in about 43 minutes, but only because its cache was warm.

**Port / Linux** is now a matrix, one job per part:

- `common`: everything except the games' programs (`OPENRAC_PORT_GAMES_IN_ALL=OFF`), plus every test without a game label, the hostgen and cache regressions, and the configuration check.
- one part per program in `port/game/*/hostgen.json` (`rac1-pal`, `rac1-ntsc`, `rac2-ntsc`, `rac2-pal`, `rac2-ntsc2`, `rac3-ntsc`, `rac4-ntsc`): `openrac-<id>`, plus its tests (`ctest -L '^game-<id>$'`).

The parts are per program rather than per game because a first run with one part per game took 53 minutes for rac2's three programs, cold. The scope job lists the parts and now runs on pushes too, so a new version gets its own p

merged.title: feat(launcher): offer the developer disc switch for every disc the launcher knows
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
The developer disc switch only looked at the games folder, so without one it never showed, even with two versions set up.

It now counts every disc the launcher knows for a game:
- images in the games folder (as before; two images of one version are still one entry)
- each version with a set-up, the one in place or one kept aside as `<game>@<version>`
- the image a version was last set up from (new `discImages` setting, developers only), while the file is still there and still identifies as that version

Switching to a version known only by its set-up needs no games folder. Choosing a version known only by its remembered image sets it up from that image. Players see nothing new, and a game with one known version still shows no switch.

Tests in `disc_choice.rs`: set-ups alone offer the switch and switch back and forth; a picked image for a second version is offered; an image that moved or is now another disc is not.

merged.title: fix(hostgen): resolve a level global's $gp view so rac2's right stick turns the camera
merged.author: Veradictus
merged.untrustedBody:
The right stick did nothing to Going Commando's camera (rac2 NTSC v1.01). R3 still worked, and the pad lines in the player's log show the right stick's bytes moving, so the input reached the game.

## Cause

The same log says `func_L00_00424F98 has no C in the port yet; it does nothing`, and later `1 functions without C were called: 779 func_L00_00424F98`. That function is the follow camera's stick read. The port's host wrapper (`port/game/rac2/host/camera_latch.c`) calls the game's version as `func_L00_00424F98__game`, and hostgen had made that a stub, so the stick value never got written and the camera never turned.

The problem came in with #341 (29f8e6142). Its rac2-decomp sync replaced the functional C for this function with the matched `src/levels/shared/L00_00424F98-g8.c`, which declares

```c
extern float ref_L00_00424F98_03 SDATA(ref_L00_00424F98_03);
```

`SDATA` labels the variable `ref_L00_00424F98_03__gp`. `Program.data_address` found level-derived names (`ref_LNN_…`) only

merged.title: fix: touch swim controls and fixed button places
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** under water the touch pad showed fire and quick select, which the game blocks there, and R1 even without the Hydro-Pack. Buttons also moved around from context to context (foot, water, Clank, menus).

**After:** under water only up (X), down (square) and, with the Hydro-Pack, R1 (in dash's place). Each pad button now has one place in every context: X in the corner, circle low left, triangle mid arc, square far left, R1 up top. Ship and jet keep their own layout.

**How:** actions can pin an arc place with a new `"at"` field (0 to 7); the rest fill the free places in order. rac1's touch.c reports a `hydro` hint while swimming with the Hydro-Pack (item_available, read only). MODS.md documents `at`.

**Tested:** touch and mod unit tests (new test for `at`), conventions, layering, before/after renders of foot, water, Clank and Giant Clank. Not run in game: diving with the Hydro-Pack.

merged.title: feat: rumble from the game's own motor commands
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** the controller never shook. libvib's `sceVibGetProfile` told the games the pad had no motors, `sceVibSetActParam` had no replacement, and Deadlocked's libpad motor calls were stubs.

**After:** Going Commando and Deadlocked shake the pad in the same places and for the same time as on the PS2, because the game's own code drives it. Ratchet & Clank stays without rumble, as on the console: its actuator code is never called, and libvib's sender is not on the disc.

**How:**
- `lib/pad.c` reports a DualShock 2 motor profile (small + large) and unpacks `sceVibSetActParam`. rac4 `pad.c` implements `scePadSetActAlign`, `scePadSetActDirect` and `scePadInfoAct`. Both go through the new `openrac_game_set_motors`.
- `platform/rumble.h` shapes the motors for modern pads. Each motor gets a spin-up and a short fade, and a motor starting from rest gets a 40 ms kick. The small motor plays at DS2 strength, with a little low-motor texture mixed into the high motor. Trigger motors are optional

merged.title: fix(rac1): co-op hits and damage reach both games
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
Before:
- In co-op, a member's wrench and weapon hits on enemies mostly never reached the host, so enemies did not die.
- Enemy shots, beams and blasts flew through the other player's character, so only melee hurt a member.

After:
- An enemy hit by a member dies in both games.
- Enemy shots aimed at a member hit that member's character and hurt them.

How:
- The collision code writes hit records straight into the hit ring and skips the PostHitMessage / record_moby_hit wraps, so mods never heard of those hits. The collision queries now note each hit they record and tell the mods once the query (and its parity check) ends.
- A figure keeps the hero's collision data with all primitives off. It is solid only while an enemy update stands that member in for the hero. Player shots never see it, so there is no friendly fire.
- Without a mod that listens for hits nothing changes: the new path returns at once.

Tested:
- Regression routes, rac1 NTSC, all 19 levels, develop vs this branch: 19 sa

merged.title: style(port): clang-format the rumble lines in the pad libraries
merged.author: nickyyOO
merged.untrustedBody:
**Before:** the Port conventions step on develop fails: three lines added by #362 (rumble) in `port/game/common/lib/pad.c` and `port/game/rac4-ntsc/host/pad.c` are not in clang-format's layout (one-line enums, wrapped signature, pointer spacing).

**After:** those lines are formatted; the step passes.

**How:** `git clang-format` (21.1.8, the CI pin) on the lines #362 changed in the two files. Whitespace only, no code change.

**Tested:** `check_conventions.py --since <base> --touched --strict-touched` with the CI's base and with #362's parent: 0 to fix. `git diff -w` is empty apart from line breaks. No build needed.

opened.title: fix(rac4): correct 18 functions the masked audit counted as matched
opened.author: farfeduc
opened.untrustedBody:
`tools/audit_matches.py` masks the 16-bit immediate of every load, store and add that is not `$sp`-based (`tools/retail.py`), so 18 functions in `src/` count as matched although their code differs from retail. Most step an `s32` pointer in bytes, as m2c writes it (`p += 4` moves 16 bytes where retail moves 4), or add a byte offset to an `s32` symbol (`(i * 0xB8) + &D_x`). `func_L01_00495838` started its delay loop at 4 instead of 5.

The pointer steps are now element counts and the byte offsets go through a `u8` pointer. Sources only: the report does not change, since all 18 were already counted.

## Verified

- Each of the 18 functions compiled with `tools/cc.sh`: every word without a relocation equals retail, and every `jal`, `%hi`/`%lo` pair and `$gp` access resolves to the address retail uses (`tools/strict_check.py`, proposed in #361). Before this change all 18 fail it.
- `venv/bin/python tools/audit_matches.py`: 243 exact, 0 not exact (overlays from `wrenchbuild unpack ... -g dl

opened.title: feat(rac4): match 289 functions
opened.author: farfeduc
opened.untrustedBody:
289 new functions, in four commits that each regenerate `progress/report.json` with their sources (the rac4 CI checks the report against `src/`):

| Commit | Functions |
|---|---:|
| core | 25 |
| network | 29 |
| resident level code | 219 |
| level overlays (L00, L01, L04, L05, L15) | 16 |

## How

Drafts from `tools/auto_structs.py` (m2c with structures built from the member accesses, four compile variants), with two fixes applied to the drafts before compiling:

- parameters m2c leaves out because the function never reads them are put back: without them every later argument moves up one register;
- m2c's byte steps on `s32` pointers become element steps, and byte offsets from a symbol go through a `u8` pointer.

Names follow `CONTRIBUTING.md`: functions by address, structures `Type1`, `Type2` ..., members by offset.

## Verified

- The collision code writes hit records straight into the hit ring and skips the PostHitMessage / record_moby_hit wraps, so mods never heard of those hits. The collision queries now note each hit they record and tell the mods once the query (and its parity check) ends.
- A figure keeps the hero's collision data with all primitives off. It is solid only while an enemy update stands that member in for the hero. Player shots never see it, so there is no friendly fire.
- Without a mod that listens for hits nothing changes: the new path returns at once.

Tested:
- Regression routes, rac1 NTSC, all 19 levels, develop vs this branch: 19 sa

opened.title: feat(metal): a Metal renderer for macOS behind OPENRAC_GL_API=metal
opened.author: xsyetopz
opened.untrustedBody:
Before:
- On macOS the port drew with OpenGL 4.1, which Apple has deprecated, or with Vulkan through MoltenVK.

After:
- `OPENRAC_GL_API=metal` draws the renderer's GL calls with Metal (`port/renderer/metal`), on Apple silicon and on Intel Macs back to 2015's (`MTLGPUFamilyMac2`, macOS 12).
- If Metal cannot open, or lacks a GL function, the log says why and the window draws with OpenGL, never MoltenVK.
- OpenGL stays the default everywhere. The enhanced renderer stays on Vulkan's render graph, so under Metal the game looks as it does on OpenGL.

How:
- Shaders are not rewritten. glslang makes SPIR-V as for Vulkan, and SPIRV-Cross writes it as MSL. Programs compile without fast math, fusing and dividing as the OpenGL beside them does.
- Depth-tested draws on Apple's GPUs are drawn in two halves, so depth comes out bit for bit as OpenGL's. AMD GPUs keep one draw of `(z + w) * 0.5`.
- New images start as Apple's OpenGL starts them. Metal opens the GPU OpenGL would use. Older GPUs (Haswel
